Per our call, I put together a first-pass set of throughput scenarios tied to the models you mentioned (opt-13b and a trimmed opt-6b variant) and a couple of SLA targets you asked about. The attached spreadsheet (catalyst_capacity_model_v1.xlsx) contains the token/sec estimates, baseline latency curves, and a simple GPU count mapping across 3 workload shapes:

- Pilot (P50 bursty): 200 reqs/min, 45% chat-style prompts, avg tokens 120 in / 60 out
- Growth (steady): 600 reqs/min, 30% chat, avg tokens 80 in / 40 out
- Enterprise (SLA): 1800 reqs/min, 60% chat, avg tokens 150 in / 80 out

Quick highlights from sheet (see tab 'summary'):
- opt-13b with 8-bit quant yields ~12k tokens/sec per GPU under continuous batching for 512-context median latency ~95ms
- opt-6b trimmed runs ~26k tokens/sec per GPU at median latency ~60ms
- For your Enterprise scenario with 99th percentile latency target <= 250ms, we estimate needing 6x A100-class GPUs for opt-13b (with conservative headroom) or 2-3x for the opt-6b variant.

Questions for you so we can firm numbers:
1) Which model(s) do you plan to serve in production vs. pilot?
2) Expected growth cadence (QTD) so we size commit vs. burst plan
3) Any hard 99th-ms SLA for public endpoints?

I copied Marcus for the runtime/latency math and Grace for commercial sizing and headroom options. If that aligns, Marcus will post a technical note on the exact assumptions and Grace will follow with pricing buckets tied to buffer levels (10/25/40% headroom).

Ben — quick technical note on the spreadsheet numbers (pulling directly from our perf harness):

Assumptions baked into the model tab:
- Model throughput measured with continuous request arrival and dynamic batching (up to 32 sequences per batch).
- Average input tokenization rates assume byte-pair encoding for your prompt mixes.
- Latency numbers are end-to-end serving (network + runtime exec + kv-cache hot hit rate 70%).

Raw per-GPU estimates (A100-like):
- opt-13b @ int8: 12,000 tokens/sec sustained, median per-token processing ~0.083ms, P99 depends heavily on tail (cold KV cache and long contexts add ~60-120ms).
- opt-6b-trim @ int8: 26,000 tokens/sec sustained, median per-token ~0.038ms.

Mapping to your Enterprise traffic (150 avg in / 80 avg out -> ~230 tokens per request):
- At 1800 req/min -> 6,900 req/hr -> ~1.6M tokens/hr -> ~450 tokens/sec aggregate.
- With opt-13b @ 12k tok/sec per GPU, nominal GPU count = ceil(450 / 12,000) = 1 GPU. But because we size for 99th percentile and headroom for bursts, recommended config = 6 GPUs under conservative SLA mapping (includes 3x burst reserve + redundancy + autoscale cushion).
- For opt-6b-trim, nominal = ceil(450 / 26,000) = 1 GPU, recommended = 3 GPUs (lower P99 tail so fewer buffers needed).

Why the gap between nominal and recommended: continuous batching amortizes GPU work, but burst arrival patterns (e.g., 20x short spikes) and KV cache miss storms increase P99. Our conservative headroom policy for enterprise commits is to provision ~4-6x the nominal for opt-13b and ~2-3x for smaller models.

I also added a small sensitivity table in the spreadsheet showing token/sec degradation with longer context windows (1k / 2k / 4k) and with degraded KV hit rates (70% -> 30%). That drives most of the P99 risk.

Happy to walk through the numbers over a screenshare — I can also export a simplified 'SLA-ready' slide with the model-level counts and failover plan.

— Marcus

Thanks team — action note and next steps below. I attached a compact SLA/price matrix (catalyst_sla_matrix_v1.pdf) with three commercial options and expected monthly cost ranges based on the modeling sheet: Pilot / Standard / Enterprise.

Summary of recommended options (short):
- Pilot (opt-6b-trim) 
  - Commit: 2 GPUs reserved (sustained), Burst pool: additional 1 GPU on demand
  - Headroom: ~25% (sufficient for early growth), Estimated monthly spend: $4.5k - $7k (includes burst usage)
- Standard (initial prod, mixed models)
  - Commit: 4 GPUs reserved (support opt-6b + small opt-13b traffic), Burst pool: 3 GPUs
  - Headroom: ~40%, Estimated monthly spend: $16k - $23k
- Enterprise (SLA-backed for opt-13b primary)
  - Commit: 6 GPUs reserved (opt-13b primary), Burst pool: 6 GPUs + 2x redundancy nodes
  - Headroom: ~60% (targets P99 <= 350ms for specified traffic profile), Estimated monthly spend: $58k - $75k + overage for extreme spikes

Fallback / routing policy (we propose):
1) Primary: opt-13b quantized (default)
2) If P95 > 220ms or P99 > 350ms: route low-priority traffic to opt-6b or pre-warmed quantized opt-13b image (automated threshold-based routing)
3) If autoscaler cannot provision within spike window: invoke ‘degrade-to-cache’ policy (short-term TTL increase + smaller contexts) and return a warning header to client

Next steps:
- Marcus: generate the 10x-for-3-minutes spike table (I flagged the sheet and added a column for cost delta).
- Ben: confirm which pricing bucket Catalyst prefers for proposal draft.
- Elena: confirm whether the fallback routing above is acceptable (and whether degraded responses must include a specific header for downstream analytics).

I’ll prepare a one-page commercial that ties the commit counts to SLA language and a DocuSign-ready MSA addendum with the burst/overage terms.

Grace O'Connor
